meta.notice: Bibliographic records marked VERIFIED were checked against PubMed (E-utilities) on 2026-11-25 and their summaries only restate what each abstract says. Records marked DEMO are fictitious sample studies for demonstration; they are NOT real research. All formulations are ILLUSTRATIVE reconstructions, not manufacturer recipes.
meta.researchNotes: Public INCI lists exist for many marketed serums and creams, but manufacturers do not disclose exact percentages. Therefore every formulation here is flagged ILLUSTRATIVE and uses round example percentages.

ingredients.name: Purified Water
ingredients.description: Solvent and base component of most cosmetic emulsions and serums. Used to bring a formulation to 100%.
ingredients.solubility: Universal cosmetic solvent for water-soluble ingredients.

ingredients.name: Glycerin
ingredients.description: Widely used humectant that attracts and retains water in the stratum corneum.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.description: Vitamin B3 derivative studied for effects on the appearance of ageing facial skin. The cited clinical study tested a 5% niacinamide formulation; this is not a recommended or proven range for other formulas.
ingredients.compatibilityNotes: Compatibility with other actives and pH must be confirmed by formulation stability testing.

sources.name: PubMed 16029679 - Bissett et al., Dermatol Surg 2005

ingredients.name: Sodium Hyaluronate
ingredients.description: Sodium salt of hyaluronic acid, a high-water-binding polysaccharide used for hydration claims. Published topical studies use different molecular weights, which affects results.
ingredients.solubility: Water soluble; viscosity rises with molecular weight.

sources.name: PubMed 22052267 - Pavicic et al., J Drugs Dermatol 2011
PubMed 24688623 - Jegasothy et al., J Clin Aesthet Dermatol 2014

ingredients.name: Panthenol
ingredients.description: Provitamin B5 used as a moisturising and skin-conditioning ingredient.

ingredients.name: Ceramide NP
ingredients.description: Skin-identical lipid used in barrier-supporting moisturisers, usually combined with cholesterol and fatty acids.
ingredients.solubility: Oil/lipid phase; needs a suitable emulsion system.
ingredients.compatibilityNotes: Lipid ratios (ceramide : cholesterol : fatty acid) influence barrier performance; confirm with finished-product testing.

sources.name: PubMed 22507050 - Draelos, Clin Dermatol 2012 (review of barrier repair creams)

ingredients.name: Cholesterol
ingredients.description: Skin-identical lipid used alongside ceramides in barrier-oriented formulations.

ingredients.name: Squalane
ingredients.description: Stable hydrocarbon emollient that softens skin and improves spreadability.

ingredients.name: Tocopherol
ingredients.description: Vitamin E, used as an antioxidant to help protect oils in a formulation.

ingredients.name: Phenoxyethanol
ingredients.description: Preservative used to protect water-containing formulations from microbial growth.
ingredients.concentrationSource: EU Cosmetics Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Annex V (maximum 1.0% as a preservative)
ingredients.regulatoryNotes: Maximum 1.0% in finished EU cosmetic products. Verify the current Annex V entry for each target market.

sources.name: EU CosIng database (ingredient and Annex V lookup)

ingredients.name: Xanthan Gum
ingredients.description: Polysaccharide thickener used to give serums and creams viscosity and suspension stability.
ingredients.solubility: Disperses in water to form viscous solutions.

evidence.title: Niacinamide: A B vitamin that improves aging facial skin appearance
evidence.population: Female white subjects with clinical signs of facial photoaging
evidence.endpoint: Fine lines and wrinkles, hyperpigmented spots, red blotchiness, yellowing, elasticity (cutometry)
evidence.methodology: Applied twice daily for 12 weeks; facial images and instrumental measures at baseline and 4-week intervals.
evidence.resultsSummary: Abstract reports significant improvements for niacinamide in fine lines and wrinkles, hyperpigmented spots, red blotchiness, skin yellowing and elasticity. The abstract does not state a percentage wrinkle reduction.
evidence.limitations: Ingredient-level (single 5% test vehicle), not the finished formulation. Single population (female, white). 12-week duration. Authors are affiliated with a cosmetics manufacturer.

evidence.title: Efficacy of cream-based novel formulations of hyaluronic acid of different molecular weights in anti-wrinkle treatment
evidence.studyDesign: Randomised, vehicle-controlled (periocular area, vehicle on the other eye)
evidence.population: Female subjects aged 30-60 with periocular wrinkles
evidence.endpoint: Skin hydration, elasticity, wrinkle depth (replica morphometry, Ra and Rz)
evidence.methodology: Twice-daily application for 60 days; measurements at baseline, 30 and 60 days.
evidence.resultsSummary: All HA creams significantly improved hydration and elasticity vs placebo. Wrinkle depth improved significantly only for the 130 kDa and 50 kDa (low molecular weight) HA groups after 60 days.
evidence.limitations: Tested 0.1% hyaluronan creams; effect depends on molecular weight. Periocular area only. Not the finished formulation under assessment.

evidence.title: Niacinamide-containing facial moisturizer improves skin barrier and benefits subjects with rosacea
evidence.studyDesign: Randomised, investigator-blind, controlled observational study (untreated forearm control)
evidence.testedSubject: A niacinamide-containing facial moisturizer (a different commercial formulation)
evidence.endpoint: Stratum corneum barrier function (instrumental and DMSO probe), hydration, rosacea severity
evidence.methodology: Moisturizer applied twice daily to face and one forearm for 4 weeks; other forearm untreated.
evidence.resultsSummary: The abstract states instruments provided objective measures of improved barrier function and hydration; it does not give numeric effect sizes.
evidence.limitations: Finished product is a different formulation with undisclosed niacinamide level. Population limited to rosacea. Observational design with untreated control.

evidence.title: Efficacy of a New Topical Nano-hyaluronic Acid in Humans
evidence.sourceName: Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology
evidence.studyDesign: Open evaluation of a product range with instrumental and rater assessment (control not described in the abstract)
evidence.testedSubject: A nano-hyaluronic acid product range (lotion, serum, cream) - a different commercial formulation
evidence.methodology: Periorbital measurements over 8 weeks plus image rating by six trained raters.
evidence.resultsSummary: Abstract reports significant moisturising effects after 2, 4 and 8 weeks and concludes wrinkle depth decreased by up to 40% and hydration increased by up to 96% at 8 weeks. The 'up to' figures are best-case values, not average effects.
evidence.limitations: Different formulation and undisclosed HA concentration. Small sample. Control group not described in the abstract. 'Up to' maxima overstate typical response.

evidence.title: New treatments for restoring impaired epidermal barrier permeability: skin barrier repair creams
evidence.testedSubject: Barrier repair creams containing ceramides, hyaluronic acid and other substances
evidence.methodology: Reviews the formulation and effect of skin barrier creams.
evidence.resultsSummary: Reviews externally applied substances such as ceramides and hyaluronic acid used to treat damaged skin barrier. The abstract is descriptive and gives no quantitative claim-level results.
evidence.limitations: Narrative review, no pooled quantitative estimate; cannot substantiate a specific numeric claim.

evidence.title: Ceramide-Containing Adjunctive Skin Care for Skin Barrier Restoration During Acne Vulgaris Treatment
evidence.studyDesign: Double-blind, controlled (ceramide cleanser + lotion vs basic cleanser)
evidence.population: Acne vulgaris patients treated with adapalene 0.3% / benzoyl peroxide 2.5% gel
evidence.testedSubject: A ceramide-containing foaming cleanser and facial lotion (different formulation)
evidence.endpoint: Transepidermal water loss (TEWL), dryness, lesion counts
evidence.methodology: Participants used the acne gel once daily plus the ceramide routine or a basic cleanser twice daily; TEWL measured over 12 weeks.
evidence.resultsSummary: Abstract states TEWL in the ceramide group remained significantly lower than control at all timepoints and improved from baseline by week 12. No numeric TEWL percentage is given in the abstract.
evidence.limitations: Acne population with irritating drug treatment, not general dry skin. Different formulation and undisclosed ceramide level. Barrier damage was induced by the acne drugs.

evidence.title: [DEMO] 4-week corneometry study of Hyaluronic Hydration Serum v1
evidence.population: Adults with normal to dry skin
evidence.methodology: Twice-daily application on the forearm for 4 weeks versus vehicle; measurements at baseline, week 2 and week 4.
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: mean hydration increased 32% from baseline at week 4, significantly above vehicle.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Single centre, forearm site only.

evidence.title: [DEMO] 2-week TEWL study of Ceramide Barrier Cream v1
evidence.methodology: Cream applied twice daily to the lower leg for 2 weeks; TEWL measured at baseline and week 2.
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: TEWL decreased 12% from baseline at week 2.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Only 2 weeks, open-label, small sample.

evidence.title: [DEMO] 4-week vehicle-controlled TEWL study of Ceramide Barrier Cream v1 (no significant difference)
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: TEWL change versus vehicle was not statistically significant at week 4.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Small sample, possibly underpowered.

evidence.title: [DEMO] 4-week profilometry of a 2% niacinamide serum (no significant wrinkle change)
evidence.methodology: Twice-daily application for 4 weeks; 3D profilometry of the crow's-feet area.
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: no significant change in wrinkle depth versus vehicle at 4 weeks.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Tested a lower concentration (2%) than the formulations under assessment and only 4 weeks.

evidence.title: [DEMO] 4-week hydration study of a 5% glycerin vehicle
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: hydration increased 18% from baseline at week 4.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Simple aqueous gel, not a finished formulation.

evidence.title: [DEMO] Instrumental emollience measurement of squalane at 2%
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: small hydration increase, no TEWL change.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Single arm, no vehicle control.

evidence.title: [DEMO] Human repeat-insult patch test of a serum preserved with 0.9% phenoxyethanol
evidence.resultsSummary: DEMO RESULT: no irritation or sensitisation reactions observed.
evidence.limitations: Fictitious demo record. Safety only; says nothing about efficacy claims.
